entries.title: Open available Fluent Kids lessons from the roadmap
entries.summary: Each available Fluent Kids lesson opens directly from its row in the dashboard roadmap.
details: Each preview has its own link. Lessons without a preview still show Planned.

entries.title: Fluent Kids previews in Lesson Material Maker
entries.summary: Fluent Kids replaces the Young Learners card in the dashboard and organizes its materials by level, unit, and lesson.
details: The preview supports separate student and tutor views and activities for ages 6–8 and 9–12.
Switch between English with Japanese translations and English-only practice. The preview supports interactive answer checks and picture reveals.

entries.title: Corrected Level 8 score-range label
entries.summary: The backend now supplies the correct TOEIC 785–940 label for Level 8 Conversational Skills.
details: The badge-only release was verified against the deployed API image. Lesson publication states and authored lesson content were unchanged.

entries.title: Elysium Mainnet network support in Engine
entries.summary: Engine supports Elysium Mainnet in network selection, contract forms, and wallet balance reads, with HYPE shown as the native gas currency.
details: The Engine API and dashboard release passed Go tests, dashboard type checks and unit tests, desktop/mobile contract-form checks, and live chain, block and native-balance reads.
This entry records network support, not a claim that connected applications or contracts were deployed by that release. Existing Arbitrum connectivity was also checked.

entries.title: Useful language restored in listening challenges
entries.summary: Configured Useful Language now appears in listening challenges across the student and tutor material views and dashboard preview.
details: Listening missions use the same configured language support as the other activity types, rather than silently omitting it.
Listening transcripts remain tutor-only. This renderer correction does not change lesson records, student notes, exercise marks, or backend APIs.
The deployed student, tutor, and dashboard builds passed desktop and mobile checks in light and dark themes.

entries.title: Managed-user wallets for queued contract writes
entries.summary: Engine can execute authorized contract writes from an active managed-user wallet within the authenticated project, alongside existing server-wallet operations.
details: The worker resolves the managed signer through Engine/Vault and rejects missing or cross-project wallets. Existing API scopes, chain and contract restrictions, and wallet locks remain enforced.
Signing credentials stay inside Engine/Vault. This is a trusted-backend capability, not permission for browser clients to choose arbitrary wallets or access project API keys.

The backend release passed its Go tests. The connected shop workflow was exercised on Arbitrum Sepolia using a separately funded test wallet; this does not enable mainnet checkout or change FluentXVerse lesson booking.

entries.title: Marketplace V3 API reference and checkout guidance
entries.summary: Engine's API reference now documents the deployed Marketplace V3 interface, including direct listings, approvals, supported currencies, checkout, and transaction polling.
details: Examples use the pinned contract ABI and Engine's string-array argument format, including JSON-encoded tuples, explicit managed signers, and idempotency keys for writes.

Listing guidance covers empty marketplaces, bounded inclusive page reads, status and time checks, ownership, and approvals. A queued HTTP response is not presented as completed payment or delivered inventory.
Desktop and mobile reference checks used mocked API calls. The documented testnet connection does not imply that every preview product has minted inventory or a live listing.

entries.title: Durable contract-write retries for score publication
entries.summary: Generic Engine contract writes now support project-scoped idempotency keys so a backend can recover uncertain submissions without creating a replacement transaction.
details: Retries with the same project, key, and transaction data return the original operation, including after API-key rotation. Reusing a key with changed transaction data is rejected.
A connected game backend uses a durable outbox to publish validated personal-best scores on Arbitrum Sepolia, with canonical receipt checks, restart recovery, and reorganization repair.

Concurrency, key rotation, historical transaction adoption, and ambiguous-response recovery were tested. Onchain publication records a backend-validated result; it is not a zero-knowledge proof of gameplay or a change to tutor-screening verification.

entries.title: Prebuilt marketplace, ERC-1155, and leaderboard templates
entries.summary: Engine gained deployment forms and APIs for pinned thirdweb Marketplace V3 and TokenERC1155 implementations, plus a publisher-controlled leaderboard contract.
details: The contract catalog exposes ABIs and upstream source references. Queued deployments retain project ownership checks, API scopes, chain restrictions, Vault signing, and receipt tracking.

Existing deployed contracts keep their original addresses and ABIs. New marketplace and collection instances use atomically initialized proxies; template changes do not upgrade historical non-upgradeable contracts.

Sample deployments, roles, marketplace routes, and leaderboard registration were checked on Arbitrum Sepolia. Upstream thirdweb fees still apply where specified; source verification and internal tests are not an independent security audit.

entries.title: Consistent tip-marker alignment across apps
entries.summary: Tip markers now align with the first line of text, including when a tip wraps onto multiple lines.
details: The same spacing correction is live in the student and tutor views and the dashboard preview.
Published styles passed desktop and mobile checks in light and dark themes. This was a visual correction only; application behavior and APIs are unchanged.

entries.title: Reliable Daily Dispatch archive and search navigation
entries.summary: Article search, archive links, and student or tutor preview modes now stay consistent as readers move between Daily Dispatch views.
details: Tutor sidebar search includes older published articles in the classroom library, rather than only the default administrative list.
Student archive navigation and dashboard student/tutor archive routes preserve the selected view when changing months or opening an article.
Desktop and mobile checks covered direct links, reloads, browser back, both themes, and student answer visibility.

entries.title: One Daily Dispatch reading experience across apps
entries.summary: Daily Dispatch articles now share a renderer, typography, theme behavior, source links, and the updated newspaper mark across the student, tutor, and dashboard apps.
details: Standalone articles and classroom frames use the same template and follow the selected light or dark theme. Student views do not expose tutor answers.
Legacy source text is displayed as readable attribution and labeled links. Opaque Google News RSS links are not assigned invented publisher names, and persisted article records are unchanged.
Published layouts, classroom frames, font controls, citations, and desktop/mobile parity passed browser checks with intercepted API fixtures.

entries.title: Feedback history removed from student navigation
entries.summary: The student app no longer links to the feedback-history page, and existing /reviews links return to Home.
details: The sidebar Feedback entry and My feedback link were removed without deleting existing records or changing backend review policies.
Live desktop and mobile checks confirmed the redirect and absence of feedback-history API requests from that route.

entries.title: Clearer mission and technology ecosystem on the website
entries.summary: The About page clarifies FluentXVerse's learning mission, and the homepage identifies the networks and providers used across the ecosystem.
details: The ecosystem section covers Arbitrum, zkVerify, Robinhood Chain, Alchemy, Privy, OpenZeppelin, and Aero, with locally served logos and links to their official websites.
Technology usage is not a claim of sponsorship, endorsement, or a formal commercial partnership.
The updated About copy and homepage section passed live asset and desktop/mobile browser checks.

entries.title: Tutor reward quotes and managed claiming
entries.summary: Tutors have a Rewards page to review released balances, request an asset quote, and confirm a sponsored claim through their managed wallet.
details: The backend binds each quote to the authenticated tutor, receiving wallet, available reward balance, token, minimum output, nonce, and deadline. Engine/Vault authorizes the exact claim without exposing signing credentials to the browser.
Uncertain submissions reuse durable authorization and idempotency records. Pending transactions are not displayed as completed before canonical success and finality checks.

Only the reviewed NVDA route was enabled initially. At rollout, the treasury and reserved reward balances were zero; no real tutor payout or paid mainnet claim was performed. Browser financial writes used controlled fixtures.

entries.title: Aero reward purchases with bounded execution
entries.summary: The reward system gained a pinned Aero adapter and a FluentXVerse-operated, Alchemy-backed price feed on Robinhood Chain.
details: Approved routes enforce exact input spending, minimum received amounts, expiry, recipient delivery checks, and cleared router allowances. Quotes fail when prices are stale or execution falls outside the configured limits.
The price feed trusts Alchemy's data and our publisher; it is not an official Alchemy oracle or a cryptographic proof of the upstream HTTPS response.

Contract receipts and runtime bindings were checked. Purchase and delivery tests used synthetic assets and an isolated mainnet fork; no real tutor funds were spent. These are internal checks, not an independent security audit.

entries.title: Monthly tutor reward administration
entries.summary: Finance staff can inspect the rewards treasury and monthly lesson totals, while superadmins can submit audited reward-period and funding operations through Engine.
details: The reward contract was deployed on Robinhood Chain, separate from the Arbitrum booking and dispute contracts. Monthly thresholds, per-lesson USD rates, and release dates are configured for future periods.

Eligibility uses reconciled completed booked lessons. Active TA-301 penalties exclude lessons, unresolved reports hold reconciliation, and finalization requires staged onchain counts to match the reviewed snapshot.

Funding, finalization, and unlocking remain explicit operations. Deployment did not choose a launch rate or pay date, fund tutor entitlements, or make a payout. Automatic recurring reward periods were not included.

entries.title: Automatic booking receipt batches of up to 32
entries.summary: Engine can publish consecutive new-booking commitments together, reducing repeated transaction overhead while keeping application booking confirmation immediate.
details: Batches contain up to 32 untouched consecutive booking events and do not wait to become full. Cancellations, amendments, disputes, and previously planned transactions preserve queue-order boundaries.
Frozen membership, saved signed bytes, and atomic finality tracking make retries reuse the original transaction rather than creating new business actions.
A live synthetic eight-booking batch was verified. This is commitment batching, not ZK-proof aggregation; no mainnet percentage gas saving or independent security audit is claimed.

entries.title: Combined booking and dispute registry on Arbitrum
entries.summary: New confirmed bookings can enter a durable background workflow for issuer-attested onchain commitments, with related amendments and disputes tied to the same opaque booking key.
details: Publication is asynchronous and does not hold up application booking confirmation. Personal identities, schedules, complaint messages, and supporting artifacts remain offchain under application access controls.
Historical bookings are not retroactively enrolled, and their existing dispute workflow remains available. Attendance, refund, and tutor compensation policies are unchanged.
The production deployment and a synthetic booking receipt were verified through canonical finalized receipts. A commitment does not independently prove attendance, teaching quality, or learning.

entries.title: Learning-first language across FluentXVerse
entries.summary: Product copy now describes FluentXVerse as an ecosystem of onchain learning applications, starting with ESL and expanding across subjects and skills.
details: The refresh covers website pages, metadata, navigation, app guides, classroom categories, and profile labels. Academic background sections use Qualifications rather than changing actual degree names.
The canonical website route is /onchain-learning, with old /onchain-education links redirected. Saved categories and database field names remain compatible with existing records.
The four frontends and scoped backend labels were deployed and checked on the active .com domains. Existing legacy domain configuration was not changed.

entries.title: Opt-in replacement lessons after tutor absence
entries.summary: Students can save an automatic-replacement preference for eligible new bookings when the original tutor is absent or misses the Present confirmation deadline.
details: The preference defaults off. A replacement requires an open, Present slot at the same lesson time and duration, with compatible language and tutor tier, before the five-minute cutoff.
A successful transfer reuses the original entitlement without a second payment. Superseded bookings retain their penalties and history; opt-out or no-match cases follow the existing refund process.

Activation is prospective, not a retroactive change to historical bookings. Isolated database and desktop/mobile checks covered preference persistence, concurrency, classroom denial, and refund idempotency.

entries.title: Private lesson dispute conversations and decisions
entries.summary: Students, tutors, and authorized staff have a structured inbox for lesson issue threads, replies, and recorded decisions, connected to the deployed dispute workflow.
details: The conversation and supporting material remain private application records. Onchain records use bounded issuer-attested commitments rather than publishing complaint messages or personal evidence.
The release preserves existing report forms, attendance rules, and refund deduplication. A receipt alone does not establish that a complaint is true or that a refund has been delivered.
Controlled browser and API checks verified access boundaries and the case lifecycle. Production configuration and receipt verification do not constitute an independent security audit.

entries.title: Consistent profile-review progress and approval states
entries.summary: Profile review now counts the same six required items across tutor screens, dashboard controls, and backend approval decisions.
details: Legacy extra keys cannot inflate progress or block completion. Repeated submissions preserve existing approved or pending status instead of creating duplicate submission notifications.
Tutor profiles display approval explicitly and refresh pending-review status while visible. Backend decisions remain authoritative; UI progress alone cannot grant approval.

entries.title: Broader dashboard activity history
entries.summary: The dashboard bell and overview show more recent operational events with links to the relevant staff screens and bounded load-more controls.
details: The feed covers persisted events across applications, identity review, interviews, lessons, reports, messages, payments, and materials, subject to the caller's access.
Sensitive documents, recordings, private proving inputs, and report descriptions are excluded from the new projections. Failed refreshes retain the previous list and offer a retry.
This is a recent activity view, not a complete immutable audit log or a reconstruction of every historical state change.

entries.title: Clearer credential status and staff verification details
entries.summary: Tutor identity screens now distinguish proof finalization, receipt availability, and completed issuance, while authorized staff can inspect credential metadata and transaction references.
details: Pending requests do not display a metadata link before finalized issuance. Historical credentials remain distinguishable from currently valid issuer approval.
Public credential metadata reads now have bounded request rates and concurrency. These protections do not make the metadata private or guarantee protection against every denial-of-service attack.
Staff tutor tables also received more compact spacing. Published layouts and focused API checks passed without changing applicant decisions.

entries.title: Production tutor identity credentials with verified issuance
entries.summary: Production identity issuance is enabled for eligible, consenting tutors, and a completed mainnet issuance has been verified through its finalized mint and recipient ownership.
details: The workflow verifies a proof on zkVerify mainnet and independently checks its official Arbitrum receipt before issuing a permanently transfer-locked credential on Arbitrum One.

Explicit production consent is required before the wallet link is published. ID images, document numbers, birth dates, and personal names are excluded from credential metadata and proof inputs; a public wallet can still be linked to a person elsewhere.
Metadata reflects current issuer approval. Historical receipts are not erased by invalidation, and wallet recovery requires support-led review rather than transferring the locked token.
This confirms the issuance workflow, not an independent security audit. The application issuer remains trusted, and metadata availability depends on FluentXVerse.

entries.title: Clearer production wallet disclosure and identity checklist
entries.summary: Tutor application guidance explains the public wallet link and separates identity review, interview approval, and credential issuance.
details: Production profile submission requires current wallet-publication confirmation. Historical test consent does not count as production consent, and draft editing remains available.
Completed identity states and application checklists have clearer labels. Scoped desktop and mobile checks passed with controlled API responses.

entries.title: Safer interview-result controls
entries.summary: The administrator interview room disables Pass and Fail controls after a result is saved, making the recorded decision clearer and preventing repeat submission from the room.
details: Corrections remain available through interview review. This dashboard update preserves the existing backend rules and does not change applicant results.
The scoped build and browser verification passed before deployment.

entries.title: Refreshed tutor homepage introduction
entries.summary: The tutor homepage has updated photo framing and horizontal supporting badges in its introductory section.
details: The original teaching scene is preserved with revised decorative positioning and responsive layouts.
Published-asset and browser checks passed. Application policies and backend behavior are unchanged.

entries.title: Identity issuance waits for a passed interview
entries.summary: A successful live ID comparison alone no longer creates an issuance-ready credential request; the bound interview must also be passed.
details: Correcting an interview result to fail cancels an unissued request. Existing pending requests were reconciled against the required gates.
This release established the approval gate without submitting a proof or mint. Production issuance was activated separately on November 3.

entries.title: ERC-1155 transfer controls appear in the Engine console
entries.summary: Engine's saved contract interface now includes transfer-policy getters and owner actions, matching the updated ERC-1155 template.
details: The correction covers new editions and the specifically verified existing collection record. Unverified legacy deployments are not assigned unsupported functions.
Console checks used synthetic data without writes. Updating the saved interface did not change an onchain transfer policy or mint a token.

entries.title: Interview entry errors explain when a room can be joined
entries.summary: Authorized applicants and staff now receive specific feedback for early entry, expired windows, and closed interview bookings instead of a generic join failure.
details: The existing fifteen-minute early-entry window and ownership restrictions remain unchanged. Unauthorized requests continue to receive generic denial.
Boundary checks and two-browser video, chat, reconnection, and retry scenarios passed with synthetic data. No interview was reopened to bypass its entry rules.

entries.title: More focused interview and identity-review workspaces
entries.summary: The staff interview room separates Identity, Evaluation, and Chat into accessible tabs, and identity review has a searchable applicant queue with clearer decision controls.
details: Video remains uncropped, call controls stay outside the scrolling tools area, and tab changes preserve drafts and notes.
Fraud rejection requires explicit confirmation; Cancel and Escape do not submit a decision. Authorized staff can inspect a cancelled interview record without reopening its media session.
Responsive review flows and two-peer interview checks passed using synthetic documents, messages, and decisions.

entries.title: A clearer ID upload and pending-review experience
entries.summary: Tutor identity screens now show submission, review, and booking progress alongside an accessible image picker, local preview, and submission checklist.
details: Applicants can preview or remove an image before submission. File-type and size guidance is clearer, with expandable retention information.
Pending-review screens separate status refresh, review-time guidance, and outcome-email information. Existing consent, review, and resubmission rules are unchanged.
Desktop, mobile, light-theme, and dark-theme checks used synthetic images rather than real identity documents.

entries.title: Clearer interview availability and application progress
entries.summary: Interview booking groups available times by date and shows the ID-acceptance deadline above the schedule, while staff application rows use consistently aligned progress steps.
details: Empty interview availability offers a single message and refresh action. Future slots are not hidden merely because the current time is in a different part of the day.
Booking confirmation, cancellation, and eligibility rules remain unchanged. Responsive booking and administrator column-alignment checks passed.

entries.title: Immediate replacement of rejected or expired ID submissions
entries.summary: Tutor applicants can submit a replacement ID immediately when resubmission is requested or a submission expires, without waiting until midnight.
details: A replacement is saved before the previous submission is retired. Cleanup failures are retried without discarding the new pending submission.
The upload form and review emails explain the updated rule. Lifecycle checks covered replacement before midnight, pending status, and removal of the rejected image.
This updates the closed-test identity-review workflow; it does not issue a blockchain identity credential.

entries.title: Clearer ID-review status and outcome emails
entries.summary: Applicants see confirmation that their ID was received, can refresh their review status, and receive queued emails when staff record a review outcome.
details: The pending screen includes interview-preparation guidance and a suggested 24-48-hour review window. This is guidance, not a guaranteed response deadline.
Review emails cover acceptance, resubmission, interview matching, and other recorded outcomes. Acceptance includes the interview-booking deadline.
Failed sends are retried. Lifecycle and desktop/mobile checks used synthetic data and mocked mail delivery; inbox delivery is not guaranteed.

entries.title: Interview preparation and clearer application review
entries.summary: Tutor applicants have a dedicated interview-preparation guide, while staff can distinguish profile approval, ID review, and interview readiness in the application workspace.
details: Application review places ID status before interview scheduling, keeping document review separate from teaching approval.
The interview guide and administrator application layouts passed desktop and mobile browser checks with synthetic API responses.

entries.title: Persistent private storage for identity documents
entries.summary: Encrypted ID submissions now persist across normal API restarts when their private storage and keys remain intact, replacing the temporary memory-only testing setup.
details: Document viewing remains restricted to authorized staff. Existing deletion deadlines and retry handling remain in place.
Live checks used synthetic uploads to verify private access, fresh-process readback, and deletion. Test files and applicant records were removed afterward.
Live deletion does not guarantee erasure from historical backups or snapshots. Identity documents are not published onchain or sent to an AI provider by this workflow.

entries.title: Private tutor identity review for closed testing
entries.summary: The tutor application workflow now supports private ID submission, staff review, and a live identity comparison during the interview in a closed-test rollout.
details: The workflow separates document acceptance, interview booking, live matching, and teaching approval, with defined expiry and resubmission states.
Authorized staff can review submitted images through private application endpoints. Verification used synthetic applicants rather than real identity documents.
Identity approval is not a wallet credential. Identity-specific zero-knowledge proofs, receipt-bound issuance, revocation, and wallet recovery remain separate work.

entries.title: Transfer controls for new Engine ERC-1155 editions
entries.summary: Engine's ERC-1155 template now supports owner-controlled transfer restrictions and an irreversible transfer lock for newly deployed editions.
details: Disabled transfers apply to single and batch operations, including approved operators. A permanent lock cannot be undone through ownership changes.
Existing non-upgradeable contracts are unchanged. Creating an edition does not automatically lock transfers, verify an identity, or implement credential recovery and revocation.
Contract and API tests passed. This template deployment did not create a new onchain collection, mint credentials, or submit a proof.

entries.title: Lesson-dispute contract template in Engine
entries.summary: Engine now offers a Lesson disputes contract template with configurable administrator and operator roles, including a shared-wallet option.
details: New instances start paused, with automatic non-response actions disabled. Local contract deployment and published dashboard checks passed; browser deployment actions used fixtures.

A subsequent integration observes isolated staging events and supports a synthetic testnet pilot. Mainnet application writes remain disabled, and the new dispute workflow has not been promoted to the public apps.
The integration records application-attested events; it does not independently arbitrate lessons or transfer refunds.

entries.title: Device cleanup after a classroom closes
entries.summary: Camera and microphone changes that finish after classroom closure now release their tracks instead of leaving a late device stream active.
details: The follow-up covers both classroom roles and both supported media providers.
Live browser checks used controlled fixtures, including a device switch resolving after the room closed. This is not a substitute for a two-person lesson test across separate networks.

entries.title: Classroom preparation and an expanded first-lesson guide
entries.summary: Classrooms can prepare a private camera and microphone preview before the lesson starts, and the tutor Home guide now covers nine steps through lesson completion.
details: Device preparation requires authorized room access. The preview does not publish media before the scheduled start, and permission failures offer a device retry.
The illustrated guide now includes material selection, saving feedback, and final submission, with screenshots in both themes. It still disappears after the first taught lesson.
Tutor interview Return Home now returns to the tutor app. Classroom device lifecycle, theme contrast, and responsive guidance passed browser checks with controlled fixtures.

entries.title: Completed and cancelled lesson reminders stop appearing as unread
entries.summary: Obsolete note reminders and cancelled-session reminders now move into read history instead of continuing to count as actionable unread notifications.
details: Reconciliation runs before filtering, pagination, and unread counting. Notifications for missing lessons no longer offer unavailable action links.
Drafts and unsubmitted edits remain actionable. Regression checks covered retained history, counts, pagination, and separation between users.

entries.title: Refreshed tutor knowledge-base guidance
entries.summary: The tutor knowledge base has refreshed guidance aligned with the current tutor workflow.
details: The update was published as a scoped tutor-frontend release, with no backend changes.
Knowledge-base tests, responsive browser checks, and published-asset verification passed. The knowledge base remains available after the first-lesson Home guide disappears.

entries.title: Clearer email-confirmation arrival guidance
entries.summary: The tutor confirmation screen now explains that the email may take one to two minutes to arrive.
details: This is a copy clarification, not a measured delivery-time improvement or an inbox-arrival guarantee. The backend was unchanged.

entries.title: Lesson dispute workflow verified in private staging
entries.summary: The revised student, tutor, and staff dispute workflow has been deployed to an isolated test environment. It is not yet available in production.
details: The staged workflow includes attendance reporting after two minutes, after-lesson tutor explanation requests, 24-hour deadlines, staff review, and separate refund decisions.
Students and tutors do not exchange case messages. Tutor explanations and image evidence remain private to staff; students can follow up privately on a staff decision.

VPS checks passed for browser-origin enforcement, deadline processing, decision permissions, encrypted image upload and authorized download. Review also corrected origin checks and application-wide error responses.
Testing used synthetic cases and controlled credits with live transfers disabled. Production rollout remains gated on confirmed email delivery and a real-account classroom pilot.

entries.title: Backend typechecking passes without error exceptions
entries.summary: All 40 previously recorded TypeScript diagnostics have been resolved in the development source. These changes have not yet been deployed to production.
details: Email composition now narrows parsed image and document values explicitly, and external alert and proof-pilot JSON responses are validated before use.
Test fixtures now match Bun's fetch API and handle potentially missing array entries. The temporary known-error allowlist has been removed from the release check.
Full backend typechecking reports zero errors. Student and tutor typechecks and 50 focused regression tests passed. Paid proof submissions were not rerun as part of this work.

entries.title: A six-step guide to your first lesson
entries.summary: New tutors can follow an illustrated guide from opening schedule slots through entering the classroom.
details: Home now includes annotated screenshots for choosing times, opening slots, confirming Present, opening a booked lesson, and entering the classroom.
Classroom-entry guidance explains the five-minute entry window and camera, microphone, and pop-up permissions.
The guide automatically disappears after the first taught lesson and supports desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.

entries.title: A more compact notification inbox
entries.summary: Tutor notifications now use a narrower layout, shorter rows, and colors aligned with the tutor workspace.
details: All and Unread filters, date grouping, and visible read and delete actions make updates easier to review.
Pagination stops when there are no more results. Failed loads and updates show errors with appropriate retry options.
Dark-mode backgrounds were corrected, including the date headings and read notification rows.

entries.title: Text chat in speaking interviews
entries.summary: Candidates and interviewers can exchange plain-text messages during the video interview.
details: Multiline messages preserve line breaks. Enter creates a new line and the Send button sends the message; file attachments are not supported.
Chat uses the interview connection, retains unsent text during reconnection, and disables sending after the interview ends.

entries.title: Clearer navigation after an interview
entries.summary: Interview rooms now have a prominent Return Home button and clearer ended-call states.
details: Leaving an active interview requires confirmation and releases the camera and microphone.
The candidate return action currently opens the student Home page. Reloading a completed interview no longer reopens camera access.

entries.title: More consistent dark-mode surfaces
entries.summary: Notification text and tutor lesson panels received targeted contrast and background fixes.
details: Student notification titles, messages, and timestamps remain readable after a notification is marked as read.
Tutor lesson-note editor attendance and assessment sections now match the modal background.
The first-lesson guide now matches the Home page background while retaining distinct controls and screenshot framing.

entries.title: Collapsed photo guidelines in Account settings
entries.summary: Profile photo guidelines now start minimized whenever Account settings opens.
details: Tutors can expand the guidelines when needed. Photo-upload and profile-editing guidance remains available in the editing flow.

entries.title: Stable schedule tab switching
entries.summary: Switching between Upcoming and Past Lessons no longer shifts the centered schedule layout.
details: Scrollbar space is reserved consistently for short empty states and longer lesson lists.

entries.title: A clearer Lesson Operations workspace
entries.summary: Administrator lesson operations now have more organized views, filters, tables, and report actions.
details: Issue-report rows were made more compact, with expandable details and evidence. Existing review permissions and refund safeguards remain in place.

entries.title: Restored analytics visibility
entries.summary: The administrator analytics page no longer gets covered by an incorrectly positioned chart fill.
details: Chart styles were scoped to prevent conflicts with other dashboard components.

entries.title: Pagination for administrator sessions
entries.summary: Administrators can browse session records in manageable pages.
details: Page controls and page-size options support desktop and mobile. Search and date-filter changes reset the current page.

entries.title: Consistent classrooms and clearer lesson panels
entries.summary: Student and tutor classrooms now share a more consistent layout, with updated chat panels, lesson notes, and recording notices.
details: Shared classroom styling keeps the two sides of a lesson visually aligned across desktop and mobile.
Lesson panels and recording notices received layout and readability improvements.

entries.title: Smoother booking setup and administrator controls
entries.summary: Booking initialization and profile booking controls were improved, with booking settings now available to administrators.
details: The student booking flow received initialization fixes and a clearer booking action on tutor profiles.
Administrator booking settings are persisted by the backend and applied to the booking policy.

entries.title: Clearer tutor profiles, qualifications, and display names
entries.summary: Tutor profiles now have improved education and qualification editing, profile guidance, and consistent public display names across discovery and administration.
details: Applicants can review profile requirements while editing their biography, photo, and qualifications.
Student-facing tutor profiles received clearer tabs, icons, and booking controls. Profile photos retain their full framing.
Public tutor nicknames are handled consistently across tutor cards, profiles, and administrator review.

entries.title: More reliable introduction video uploads and playback
entries.summary: Tutor introduction videos now have clearer upload feedback and more reliable playback in student profiles and administrator review.
details: The server measures uploaded video duration and enforces the 30-second limit, including rejection of corrupt media.
Video streaming responses were corrected to support seeking and partial-content playback.
Upload guidance, pending-video states, and profile review controls were improved.

entries.title: Clearer application progress and interview scheduling
entries.summary: Tutor application review and interview booking now have clearer progress states, more compact lists, and improved calendar handling.
details: Interview time periods and booking dates received timezone checks, with responsive calendar and appointment-state coverage.
Administrator application and interview views now make applicant progress and review actions easier to scan.
Interview waiting, feedback, and result displays received layout improvements.

entries.title: Restored social sign-in from guest booking
entries.summary: Guest booking now opens the configured student social sign-in flow, with corrected public build settings and booking initialization.
details: The deployed student build includes the public authentication configuration required by the sign-in dialog.
Guest booking and booking initialization passed browser checks.

entries.title: Readable Business English material footers
entries.summary: The Business English course label and copyright text now use a brighter color against the dark material footer.
details: The same contrast improvement was deployed to student, tutor, and administrator material views.
Desktop and mobile previews were checked after deployment.

entries.title: Authentication required across dashboard previews
entries.summary: All dashboard routes, including standalone material previews, now require an administrator session.
details: Published lesson-detail and lesson-list APIs also require a valid administrator, tutor, or student session and use private, non-cacheable responses.
Live checks covered blocked anonymous access and continued material access for authenticated users.

entries.title: Workplace Communication curriculum workspace
entries.summary: Administrators can create and edit Workplace Communication materials in a dedicated curriculum workspace.
details: Prepare and Perform material templates have their own persisted document structure.
Workplace Communication is maintained separately from the existing Business English curriculum.

entries.title: Certification checks across tutor workspace tabs
entries.summary: Profile, Performance Metrics, and Knowledge Base now require application approval, alongside scheduling, classrooms, and teaching materials.
details: Restricted navigation and direct links return applicants to their teaching journey with a Certification Required warning.
Applicants can still complete Application Profile from the teaching journey, without access to performance statistics.

entries.title: Daily Dispatch article generation restored
entries.summary: The cloud article generator is running again, scheduled for 3:00 AM Philippine time each day.
details: The worker retries failures and catches up the most recent due day after a restart.
Daily article identifiers prevent restart retries from replacing or duplicating an already generated article. The first restored publication was verified in the classroom library.

entries.title: Simpler read-aloud speaking assessment
entries.summary: New speaking assessments contain ten read-aloud sentences, replacing the previous mix of speaking tasks.
details: AI evaluation compares the submitted transcript with the assigned sentence. Pronunciation and acoustic delivery still require human review.
AI scores are provisional and do not by themselves determine the final tutor application decision.
Written exam options are shuffled before an attempt is saved, and reading-question review now checks for more plausible distractors.

entries.title: Branded tutor confirmation emails
entries.summary: Tutor application emails now include the FluentXVerse logo, a clear confirmation button, and a clickable backup link in a mobile-friendly layout.
details: The logo is embedded in the message rather than loaded from a tracking URL. A plain-text alternative is included.
Real delivery and the confirmation flow passed checks, including single-use links and resend cooldowns. Previously delivered emails remain unchanged.

entries.title: Clearer written exams and stronger question checks
entries.summary: The written exam has an updated responsive design and additional AI review before newly generated questions are published.
details: Vocabulary options must fit the sentence verbatim, including tense, agreement, and passive voice. Grammar and reading items receive structural and answer-consistency checks.
A separate reviewer call checks questions without seeing the answer key. Flagged items undergo bounded revision; the exam timer starts only after acceptance. Existing attempts are not rewritten.
Desktop and mobile checks passed in both themes, alongside a live generation, answer-saving, and resume test. AI review reduces errors but does not guarantee linguistic correctness.

entries.title: Email confirmation before tutor assessments
entries.summary: Tutor applicants must confirm their email address before accessing the written assessment.
details: Confirmation messages are sent from tutor@fluentxverse.com. Links expire after 30 minutes, work once, and are protected by resend cooldowns.
The assessment gate is enforced by the backend. Live checks covered blocked unverified access, successful confirmation, and rejection of a reused link.
Administrators can access the shared tutor application mailbox from the dashboard.

entries.title: More recognizable Engine controls and browser tabs
entries.summary: Engine now has a dedicated blue terminal favicon and a compact save control beside the proof-destination selector.
details: The save icon includes a tooltip and an accessible label, with desktop and mobile layout checks.
The favicon matches Engine's terminal mark and was checked at browser-tab sizes.

entries.title: Restored zkVerify mainnet account lookups
entries.summary: Fixed the Engine verification-account error by correcting production module imports and aligning the native RPC settings with zkVerify mainnet.
details: Production Node runtime checks now cover worker imports. The network identity check remains enforced.
Three consecutive authenticated account reads returned successfully through the public Engine service. No funds were moved or paid proofs submitted during these checks.

entries.title: Project-wide proof-receipt destination selection
entries.summary: Each Engine project can select Base, ApeChain, Arbitrum One, OP Mainnet, or Robinhood Chain as its mainnet proof-receipt destination. Verification remains on zkVerify.
details: Modules inherit their root project's selection. Existing proofs retain their original destination, and Horizen is not offered for new selections.
Approved module policies cannot be silently changed. FluentXVerse's current modules remain pinned to Base until a coordinated policy migration.
Persistence, project isolation, permissions, desktop and mobile layouts, and finalized bridge reads passed checks. A paid proof-and-relayer pilot was not run on every destination.

entries.title: Safer handling for uploads and intensive requests
entries.summary: The backend now checks access earlier and applies bounded request sizes and capacity limits to uploads and proof-related requests.
details: Unauthorized upload requests are rejected before their files are processed.
Request-protection regression checks passed on the deployed backend. These controls do not guarantee protection against every network attack.

entries.title: Session handling across student and tutor apps
entries.summary: Improved authentication handling when multiple FluentXVerse apps are open in the same browser.
details: Backend requests use the session belonging to the appropriate app rather than another app's session.
Automated checks cover mixed student, tutor and administrator sessions. A new live Google sign-in and lesson test was not part of this release check.

entries.title: Base becomes the active proof-receipt destination
entries.summary: FluentXVerse's five Engine projects now use Base mainnet. Proof verification remains on zkVerify mainnet, with official bridge receipts checked on Base.
details: Screening setup verification completed under the Base configuration. Historical transactions retain their original network.
Archived contract workflows and confidential payout settlement remain disabled. A new paid proof was not submitted as part of the migration check.
